summary.headline: The Trails Committee finalized preparations for an upcoming Peninsula Trail work party and prepared its Phase 2 CPA funding application.
summary.summary: The Southborough Trails Committee met virtually to plan trail blazing and wayfinding for the Peninsula Trail along Massachusetts Water Resources Authority property. The committee also coordinated logistics for an upcoming trail building work party off Boston Road, including volunteer safety, tool prep, and parking arrangements with Sanofi. Additionally, members discussed updates to their Community Preservation Act application for Phase 2 bridge construction ahead of the June 30 deadline and evaluated purchasing promotional event banners.

topics.title: Yoga on the Trails program review
topics.summary: The committee reviewed the recent kickoff of the Yoga on the Trails program held the previous weekend. Approximately 20 participants attended the outdoor session led by the instructor. Members noted the event was successful and discussed minor adjustments to future event registration confirmations.
key_details: Around 20 participants attended the inaugural session.
National Grid work mats in the area did not disrupt the event.
The next scheduled session is in July.
topics.outcome: Discussion only; program will continue as scheduled.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee reviewed and approved meeting minutes from earlier sessions. Members noted updates regarding boardwalk materials and minor administrative adjustments.
key_details: Reviewed minutes from January 27, 2026, and June 1, 2026.
Added standardized disclaimer note regarding documents shared during meetings.
topics.outcome: Minutes of January 27, 2026, and June 1, 2026, approved as amended.

topics.title: Peninsula Trail signage and wayfinding
topics.summary: The committee evaluated signage and trail markers needed along the Peninsula Trail and its overlap with the Boroughs Loop and Aqueduct trails. Because much of the corridor follows an open MWRA access road without nearby trees, members discussed how to mark routes without cluttering the path or obstructing maintenance mowers.
key_details: Identified the need for an entry welcome sign near the ADA parking area off Boston Road.
Discussed installing low quarter-mile marker posts similar to cross-country running trail markers.
Noted the need for directional arrows where trails diverge from MWRA restricted service areas.
Considered utilizing existing metal fence posts and aluminum signs to avoid digging unnecessary post holes.
topics.outcome: Committee agreed to field-assess sign locations during the upcoming work party before purchasing additional posts.

topics.title: Trail work party logistics and safety
topics.summary: Members finalized logistics for an upcoming trail maintenance work party scheduled for Saturday morning. Volunteer work will focus on building out a new section of natural surface trail and clearing brush and poison ivy from two older segments.
key_details: Work party scheduled for Saturday, June 13, starting at 8:00 AM.
Sanofi granted permission for volunteer vehicle parking along Route 30.
Amber Stearns, trail coordinator for AMC and the Bay Circuit Trail, will attend to supervise trail building.
Volunteers will be supplied with Tyvek suits and washing stations due to prevalent poison ivy along parts of the trail.
topics.outcome: Logistics finalized for the Saturday work session.

topics.title: Peninsula Trail Phase 2 CPA funding application
topics.summary: The chair gave an update on the upcoming Community Preservation Act application deadline for Phase 2 of the Peninsula Trail project. The committee is working to secure updated engineering quotes and stakeholder letters of support for the proposed bridge and boardwalk.
key_details: Application is due June 30, 2026.
Seeking an updated scope and quote from engineering firm Beals and Thomas for bid preparation and construction oversight.
Collecting updated letters of support from town boards and state entities.
Exploring wood decking instead of composite decking on the prefabricated bridge structure to contain costs.
topics.outcome: Chair will continue compiling application materials ahead of a June 25 review meeting.

topics.title: Town Tercentennial celebration participation
topics.summary: The committee discussed an invitation from Southborough's Tercentennial Committee to participate in town celebration activities planned for next year. Members supported the idea of hosting a trail walk or historical hike highlighting town paths.
key_details: Celebration marks Southborough's 300th anniversary in 2027.
Proposed activities include a Trail Awareness Day or guided historical trail walk.
topics.outcome: Committee indicated interest in participating and will coordinate with the Tercentennial Committee as planning advances.

topics.title: Committee event banner flag purchase
topics.summary: Members discussed purchasing a portable promotional feather or teardrop banner flag using remaining funds from the current fiscal year budget. The banner will be displayed at town events such as Heritage Day, volunteer trail workdays, and Yoga on the Trails.
key_details: Targeting a 10-foot tall double-sided flag with a collapsible folding X-base for easy transport.
Flag will feature the Southborough Trails Committee logo in official committee colors.
Committee opted against specific event taglines so the flag can be reused across different programs.
topics.outcome: Chair will research vendor options and prices for a double-sided flag and folding base.
